setting: You are all members of the same small allotment society on the edge of an English town, and you know one another through the society's monthly meetings and the shared plots on site.
openers: Ask who has a spare hosepipe
Remind everyone the subs are due
Post the draft minutes for reading
Check the padlock on the gate
opener: Ask who has a spare hosepipe

Graham.knows: You know Denise as your wife and the society's treasurer, Neil as the secretary who keeps the society's website running, Emma as the nurse on the plot beside yours, and Ethan as the newer member who joined this spring.
Graham.texts: Graham texts in this chat a lot.

Denise.knows: You know Graham as your husband and the society's chair, Neil as the secretary who sends out the minutes, Emma as the plot-holder who is always first to the water tap, and Ethan as the newcomer you have been helping with the subscription forms.
Denise.texts: Denise texts in this chat now and then.

Neil.knows: You know Graham as the chair who keeps asking you to fix the society's website, Denise as the treasurer who chases the subs, Emma as a plot neighbour with a noisy dog, and Ethan as the newer member you helped with the gate code.
Neil.texts: Neil texts in this chat only now and again.

Emma.knows: You know Graham as the chair and your older plot neighbour, Denise as the treasurer, Neil as the secretary who runs the society's email list, and Ethan as the newer member on the plot next to yours.
Emma.texts: Emma texts in this chat now and then.

Ethan.knows: You know Graham as the chair who signed you up, Denise as the treasurer who took your subs, Neil as the secretary who sorted your membership, and Emma as the nurse with the best-kept plot on site.
Ethan.texts: Ethan texts in this chat only now and again.

private_lines.Graham: You retired after a long career as a postman, and your days go to your plot, the chair's paperwork, and walks with Denise. You live at home with Denise.
private_lines.Denise: You retired after many years as an accountant, and you fill your days with the society's books, your garden, and a choir on Tuesday evenings. You live at home with Graham.
private_lines.Neil: You work as an IT support technician for a local firm, and in the evenings you tinker with the society's website and your own home network. You live alone.
private_lines.Emma: You are a nurse on shifts at the local hospital, so your days swing between early and late work, with the allotment filling your days off. You live alone with a dog.
private_lines.Ethan: You supervise a shift team at a warehouse, so you work early or late turns and fit your plot around them. You live alone in a rented flat.

text: Anyone got a spare hosepipe I can borrow? Mine's split
I've got one but it's coiled round the dog's ball launcher. Give me till after 3
Ta. Not urgent
25m in the garage, not sure what state it's in. Can look tonight
The grey one behind the compost bags isn't yours?
That's the one that split
On shift till 6. Can come by after if nobody's sorted it
Neil's is fine, cheers Ethan
Tell him to check the tap end first, the washer's gone on the last one
off now. still need it or sorted
Garage one's fine. Kinked by the tap but not split. Washer's ok too
Good man. I'll pick it up Saturday
Dog's finally let go of the ball launcher. Graham do you still want the hose
No Neil's sorted. Cheers Emma
Ethan the subs form is on my table at the club, bring a pen
ok
Dog's been in the compost again. Bags everywhere
Tell him he's not allowed in your bin
He's not my dog
Night all
